verifiers.reason: The document-tool crash increment does not prove the complete native-state obligation. Prove native identities/checkpoints/usage and dynamic foreground/background graphs remain authoritative across restart. Host business obligations are distinct. Cancellation request/acknowledgement/unconfirmed termination cannot invent a terminal native outcome.

verifiers.claim: Covered direct/aliased Harness construction outside the owned factory. Workspace/observer acquisition and arbitrary lifecycle effects remain unproved.

verifiers.reason: Attach/detach a real borrowed Harness without opening/closing/resetting/aborting/reconfiguring unrelated work. Extend composition evidence to shared workspaces/watchers/transports, partial acquisition rollback, safe release and verified reattachment. Closing a viewer does not stop background execution; setup closes only what it owns.

verifiers.claim: Known reserved native task/doc declarations and alternate kernel-class mutants. Optional installation, locality and deliberate native overrides remain unproved.

verifiers.reason: Use plain Pi; install questions, validation/repair and delivery independently with native registration. Recover a pending question without another coordinator. Add/remove unrelated features without changing native defaults or existing work; preserve supported deliberate native overrides and fail accidental Boring collisions explicitly.

verifiers.claim: Private/unexported imports, covered mutation and fork/patch/version mutants. Semantic misuse and preservation of native provider capabilities require runtime proof/review.

verifiers.reason: Use supported public APIs including native FileSystem/Shell/ExecutionEnv instead of duplicates. Prove host policy, truthful denial/unsupported outcomes and recovery. Missing strict admission/publication guarantees block that composition, not unrelated native features. No per-HTTP-attempt claim without a demonstrated seam.

verifiers.claim: Package/type-only direction and forbidden runtime imports. Additional composition-policy fixtures run in npm test. Neither establishes installability, bundle safety or independent runtime behavior.

verifiers.reason: Prove the remote-coding, browser-absent background-app and assistant-sidecar recipes plus independent viewer/resource use. Reuse browser-safe resource types directly; no kernel/server FS in browser UI bundles (only an opt-in agent worker bundle may run the kernel) or mandatory heavy feature. Pure provider adapters need no agent startup; file-only tools need no dummy exec; swapping providers preserves required semantics or refuses qualification.

verifiers.claim: Dependency boundaries keep files separate from native process imports. Namespace/view coherence, paired acquisition and publication semantics remain unproved.

verifiers.reason: Prove coherent same-view direct/native/Bash/Git access on one provider acquisition; distinct published and task-private views remain isolated. Wrong namespace/incarnation pairing fails. Shell/alias/.git writes cannot bypass grants. Working scratch writes need no false domain receipts; authoritative publication is separately conditional. Cleanup/restart cannot silently substitute workspaces or stop other consumers; no native fallback.

verifiers.claim: Prompt assembly with and without the option over the same workspace file: without selfEvolving the native instructions are last and nothing from .agent/ is shown; with it the per-workspace extension is selected.
A subagent (an agent without the option) over the same workspace, with .agent/AGENTS.md present, is offered no reload tool and receives no agent-written section.
npm run check scans packages/ and examples/: no eval, Function or node:vm, and no import()/require() of a computed module; named mutants are refused. Bounded structural evidence, not data flow.
An agent-written tool that prints its environment runs through the virtual workspace exec and sees none of the studio process variables (a fictional secret set for the run).
Prompt assembly order: the host instructions are the first section and whole, the labelled, size-capped agent-written section is appended after them.
The system context the scripted model receives, and the native transcript, show the host instructions first and the labelled agent-written section last.
npm run check: the self-evolution module changes tools only through the native registry install/uninstall, with no registry of its own and no registry reads; named mutants are refused.

Write a tool, reload, the next turn is offered and calls it; broken JSON is reported while the other tool works; a full restart keeps it; deleting the files and reloading removes it; the person /reload gives the same report.
